Content: This game is a far cry from what fnaf was. The horror is poorly missing from these later games. The designs and oversaturation of the new animatronics is sad tbh. Makes the original animatronics less and less scary each new game and when every animatronic goes bad you start to think about the ineptitude of these companies (or are they all just evil). Imo it ruins the uniqueness and mystique of the originals. Its more like the horror is big corporations rather than the animatronics themselves. And the buildings are laughably huge and complex in size and layout. It's more like poppy's playtime than fnaf. I understand the formula had to change, and I like the idea of these open areas... it's not even like this is a bad game necessarily..... it's just not scary and shouldn't carry the fnaf name. Feels like it's more to sell toys and merch than a horror franchise these days

Content:
During that car parking story, I felt everything he said. Yes I never experienced the car parking experience when ppl rush you so they can hurry and park, but ppl will try to mess over you if you show any signs of niceness or friendliness and use it to their advantages. It can be from jobs, so called “friends”, relationships, family, or etc etc. Hearing and seeing what happened during Cory’s situation reminded me a lot of me. I’m not that person to get upset and riled up easily. It takes a lot for me to get upset and I’ve never nor anyone else has ever seen me upset. I’ve been thru so much when I was a kid being spoiled from a baby up to a kid seeing my parents argue and fight and also started to open my eyes on how the world really is. Moving back and forth from state to state switching schools from 4th grade - 10th grade being bullied/made fun of from kids picking on me (from 4th grade - 8th grade). Never told my parents I’ve been bullied/made fun of bc they expect me to stand up for my self, yet I wasn’t like that. I didn’t like fighting nor did I ever wanted to fight anyone. Even my teacher who watched me everyday go thru that in class pulled me to the side and asked if I wanted to call my parent/s, but I didn’t want to bc I knew if I were to say yes, I felt like my parents would be upset at me for not sticking up for myself. I sucked my tears up and just went home like nothing happened. As I got to high school (9th grade), ppl looked at me different and wanted to be my “friend” (yes the bullies too). I’ve graduated 2024 and I see a diff pov of this generation and this world. Mean ppl in this world are either ppl who are born to be cruel and mean or they are going through a hard time as well and want to take their anger out on you. 

What I’m trying to say is don’t let anybody mess with you or test you bc it will make you seem weak and vulnerable to them. If you’re getting bullied or going thru anything, talk to someone. Don’t let it build up. 




Sorry if this is really long to read.  When Cory explained that story, knowing Cory and watching him throughout these years since 2014-15, Cory is another nice person like me who’s just tired of ppl pushing our buttons. Nice ppl are smart and know what they’re capable of. But we have hearts and we don’t have terrible personalities. We don’t like harming anyone UNLESS you really push us there from what we’ve been through.

Sorry again 😅 for this incredibly long essay. Whoever is going through tough times, you are strong and you matter and your not alone❤️🙌🏾✝️💯 God bless all Samurai brethren and sisters out there ✝️

EDWIN LORE EXPLAINED :Edwin was a brilliant engineer and architect who showed a fascination with machines from a young age.
He started his own company, "Murray Co.", focused on automated solutions, and achieved some success with a robotic vacuum cleaner.
He was married to Fiona, who tragically died during childbirth.
Edwin faced financial difficulties after his business declined and eventually sold his company to Fazbear Entertainment, becoming their contractor. 
The Mimic and Personal Tragedy:
Creator of the Mimic: Edwin created the Mimic, a prototype animatronic endoskeleton with learning capabilities, to help entertain and care for his son, David.
David's Death and Edwin's Grief: David tragically died in a car accident, and Edwin, consumed by grief and anger, physically attacked the Mimic, damaging it severely and inadvertently imbuing it with his negative emotions ("agony").
Disappearance: Edwin subsequently disappeared, and Fazbear Entertainment took possession of his factory and the damaged Mimic. 
Later Life and Fazbear Entertainment:
Return to Fazbear Entertainment: Years later, Edwin returned to Fazbear Entertainment, eventually becoming a member of the Board of Directors.
The Storyteller Project: Edwin disagreed with Mr. Burrows' plan to automate the creative process for the Mega Pizzaplex using a program called "The Storyteller", which Edwin suspected was based on the Mimic1 program.
Edwin's Fate: Edwin attempted to interfere with The Storyteller but was trapped and died inside the structure, likely from asphyxiation. 
Connection to "Secret of the Mimic" Game:
The game "Secret of the Mimic" takes place at Edwin Murray's former factory, Murray's Costume Manor.
The player, a Fazbear employee, is sent to retrieve the Mimic, implying that the game's events occur sometime after Edwin's disappearance but before the events in the Mega Pizzaplex. 
Key Points Regarding Edwin:
He is portrayed as a brilliant but troubled inventor, haunted by the loss of his son.
His actions and grief led to the Mimic becoming a dangerous and malevolent force.
He is ultimately a victim of his own creation and the ruthless nature of Fazbear Entertainment.

Author: @BarbieGirlFan133
Content:
Fnaf will never be the same. Fnaf went from a time based horror game where you had to watch for a couple of anamatronics, fairly simple yet super difficult to some, to an almost free rome type game with more lore than horror, in my opinion. Ever since I'd say fnaf 6, sister location, the game has changed a lot. It went from a simple game with a few mechanics to a whole other game, basically, and security breach for me sealed the old simple fnaf that we all used to know. Ever since poppy play time chapter 1, horror games have become more like puzzles and lore rather than actual horror most of the time. The fnaf lore has always been insane so no much changes there, but in security breach especially you could do so much, and there's so many different ways to do things, like endings, that it's basically just a task simulator. I appreciate them trying to go back to the classic fnaf sometimes in games but the overall horror industry is changing for the bigger names. (Newer) Fnaf and poppy play time, 2 very popular and very well known horror games/franchises, are super similar now focusing
 more on lore or puzzles rather than typical or sensual horror.

Content: Context: This game takes place before any of the games (1979), set in Edwin Murray's facility. Edwin Murray in the books was tasked with turning the fabric suits from fall fest (a carnival owned by William Afton), into animatronics. Being an overworked father, he didn't have much time to spend time with his 4 year old son. So, he created the mimic. As stated in the office, it has the ability to copy behaviors and personas of other people. However, one day, Edwins son got ran over by a car. But the mimic still copied the boys actions, making Edwin furious. In a fit of rage, he beat the mimic, tearing its body apart. But it survived, and now, it was copying Edwin's violent actions against anyone it saw. Edwin disappeared, and fazbear entertainment went to collect what was theirs. The mimic was still at the facility though, and the people sent there were killed by it. It's also the thing that lured Cassie with Gregory's voice in ruin. Fiona went to fall fest because she felt something was wrong, only for it to burn down while she was there and she died. Also, the white tiger cory sees is named tiger rock, it's a plushie that David had (his favorite) before he died and the mimic therefore uses its appearance. In the books it actually controlled the pizzaplex. I did some researching, $25 in 1979 is equal to $110.79 today. Specifically, it belongs to the Poaceae family, a vast and diverse group encompassing roughly 10,000 different species that collectively constitute nearly 30% of all plant life on Earth. Grass plants, in their typical form, exhibit a characteristic structure composed of leaves, stems, and roots. The leaves, often referred to as blades, extend outward from a sheath-like base that encircles the plant's stem. The stem itself, also known as the culm, is generally cylindrical and features distinct nodes or joints where the leaves emerge. The root system, which can be shallow as in common lawn grasses, or deep and fibrous, serves to anchor the plant and absorb essential water and nutrients from the soil. Grasses can be classified by their lifespan: annuals, which complete their life cycle in one year, or perennials, which can live for several years. Reproduction can occur both sexually, through the production of inconspicuous flowers and seeds, and vegetatively, through modified stems such as stolons, which creep above ground, or rhizomes, which spread horizontally underground. Identifying different grass species often involves examining features like the ligule and auricles in the collar region where the leaf blade meets the sheath.
